# **1\. The movement in thirty seconds**

**REJECTIONISM** is a satirical art movement that turns rejection—professional, artistic, romantic, bureaucratic, or existential—into public evidence, visual propaganda, mythology, and collective comedy.

It is not motivational content about “learning from failure.” It is the opposite: a magnificently over-serious cultural movement built from the humiliating, ordinary fact of being told **no**.

## **Canonical language**

| Element | Canon |
| :---- | :---- |
| English name | **REJECTIONISM** |
| Italian name | **RIFIUTAZIONISMO** |
| Main descriptor | **The art movement nobody applied for.** |
| Secondary line | **The revolution that was never shortlisted.** |
| Latin motto | **AD NIHILUM** |
| Campaign line | **Rejected. Unqualified. Unstoppable.** |
| Papal name | **Pope Rejectus IV** |
| Papal style | **His Holiness Pope Rejectus IV, Supreme Pontiff of the Holy Rejection and Vicar of the Unshortlisted** |
| Papal motto | **Applica et Reicere.** |
| Papal sign-off | **E se lo dice Papa Rejectus...** |
| Final response | **Thank you for your consideration. Please keep our details on file for future opportunities.** |

## **Voice**

* Revolutionary propaganda delivered with complete bureaucratic seriousness.  
* Bitter, absurd, theatrical, and self-aware.  
* Never generic “resilience” inspiration, corporate wellness, or LinkedIn optimism.  
* The joke points upward at the cult of success and systems of rejection—not downward at vulnerable people.

## **Visual DNA**

* Constructivist red, black, and warm paper/cream.  
* Huge type, hard diagonals, decisive cut-paper geometry, sunbursts, rejected documents, closing doors, and the defeated walking figure.  
* Rough print texture is welcome; glossy corporate polish is not.  
* Keep emblems readable at small sizes. Fine illustrative detail belongs in posters and lore, not in logos.  
* The Church is the deliberate exception: aged Orthodox/medieval iconography, gold leaf, devotional composition, and historical absurdity.

## **Founding mythology**

* **Alfonso Florio** — co-founder; the masked hero who gained powers after the 200th final-stage rejection.  
* **Michele** — co-founder and **The Grand Architect of No**; the brilliant graphic designer praised and rejected by major brands including Ferrari and Benetton.  
* **Pope Rejectus IV** — formerly **Valeriano da Scalcagna**; Vicar of the Unshortlisted, based on Valerio Bindi / Valerio Sciatto: brilliant, broke, and incapable of selling out. Public material uses the papal name.  
* **The Church of the Holy Rejection** — the sacred mythology of unanswered applications, polite refusals, miraculous poverty, and eternal non-selection.  
* **The Ministry of Rejection** — the fake official institution that issues decrees, forms, propaganda, certificates, and administrative disappointment.

## **Recommended page maps**

### **rejectionism.co.uk**

1. / — the whole movement in one forceful page at launch.  
2. /manifesto — readable web edition plus designed download.  
3. /founders — the two founders and their origin stories.  
4. /institutions — Ministry, Church, and Pope Rejectus IV.  
5. /press — only after the launch: one-paragraph description, logos, founder images, and contact.

Do not build a CMS or a maze of empty pages before launch. A strong single page is better than twelve unfinished routes.

### **archiveofno.com**

1. / — selected entries, explanation, search, and submit CTA.  
2. /submit — paste text or upload an image/document; add the story; choose public name, pseudonym, or anonymous.  
3. /no/\[slug\] — permanent, shareable entry.  
4. /browse — filters by type, subject, year, and country; not by humiliating corporate taxonomy.  
5. /guidelines — privacy, redaction, permission, moderation, and takedown.  
6. Private moderation queue — approve, redact, request changes, reject, or remove.

Registration remains optional. An account may later let someone edit or claim their entries, but it must never block the first submission.

### **mor-gov.org**

1. Ministry home and seal.  
2. Decrees and announcements.  
3. Official forms, certificates, and downloadable propaganda.  
4. Selected campaigns/posters.  
5. Ministry shop only after demand exists.

### **Church**

Launch it as a section of rejectionism.co.uk, not as another standalone site. Give it a domain only when the Church produces enough recurring material to justify one.

## **Cross-linking rule**

Every site must make the ecosystem obvious:

* Rejectionism explains.  
* Archive of No collects and gives people something to share.  
* Ministry entertains and distributes.  
* Church deepens the lore.

All roads eventually lead to **Submit your rejection**.

## **D. Naming convention from now on**

Current filenames such as offocial logo.png, ministry of rejection\#.png, and timestamped ChatGPT names are not a usable archive.

Use:

brand\_asset\_variant\_ratio\_version.ext

Examples:

* rejectionism\_logo\_primary-seal\_square\_v1.svg  
* rejectionism\_banner\_founders\_16x9\_v1.png  
* mor\_logo\_red-horizontal\_v1.svg  
* church\_key-art\_holy-rejection\_4x5\_v1.jpg  
* campaign\_they-said-no\_4x5\_v1.png

Never overwrite an approved file with a different composition. Increase the version and record the change here.

# **5\. Manifesto publishing rule**

The full manifesto is intentionally ferocious, but its references to knives, blood, burning, and broken throats can be read as literal threats when stripped from the artwork. Posting the raw text everywhere is a bad distribution strategy: platforms may suppress it, journalists may misread it, and the satire will reach fewer people.

Use two editions:

* **Uncensored canonical art edition:** complete manifesto, clearly framed as satirical art, downloadable and printable.  
* **Public/platform edition:** shorter homepage and social version that preserves the anger and comedy while removing literal violent imagery.

This is not softening the movement. It is packaging the same weapon so it survives distribution.

# **6\. Archive of No: non-negotiable product principles**

The Archive is the mechanism that can turn a funny project into a movement.

1. **Submission before registration.** No compulsory account wall.  
2. **Anonymous by default, identity by choice.** Public name, pseudonym, or anonymous.  
3. **Redaction before publication.** Remove private email addresses, phone numbers, application IDs, signatures, and uninvolved staff details.  
4. **Human moderation.** Do not auto-publish accusations, personal data, threats, or defamatory claims.  
5. **Permanent share page.** Every approved rejection gets a good-looking URL and share card.  
6. **Story plus artefact.** The letter is evidence; the submitter’s short story is what makes it human.  
7. **Clear consent and takedown.** Submitters confirm they have the right to share; provide a simple correction/removal route.  
8. **Do not optimize humiliation.** No leaderboards for “worst loser,” no rating people’s pain, and no employer harassment machinery.  
9. **Seed before launch.** An empty archive looks dead. Publish at least 25 varied, approved entries before inviting strangers.  
10. **Exportable archive.** Preserve originals privately, public redacted derivatives separately, and keep metadata portable.

# **7\. Steps for world domination**

## **Phase 0 — Establish the regime (now)**

**Goal:** remove ambiguity and create production-ready foundations.

* Declare official logo and slogan.png the primary seal and offocial logo.png the narrative variant—or record a different final decision here.  
* Commission Michele/the Grand Architect to redraw the primary identity as real vector artwork.  
* Rename and classify every asset; move superseded variants into an archive rather than deleting them.  
* Confirm ownership, renewal dates, DNS, analytics, email, and deployment for all four domains.  
* Add the Facebook URL and reserve matching handles where worthwhile.  
* Produce the designed manifesto and platform-safe excerpt.

**Exit condition:** one approved identity pack, one current asset index, domains controlled, and no argument about which logo is official.

## **Phase 1 — Raise the flag (week 1\)**

**Goal:** make the movement intelligible and linkable.

* Launch the strongest possible single-page version of rejectionism.co.uk.  
* Use the primary movement banner, short explanation, founders, manifesto, visual highlights, and one dominant Archive CTA.  
* Add basic analytics, social metadata, fast images, accessibility, and a press contact.  
* Point defensive domains to their canonical destination.

**Exit condition:** a stranger can understand the joke, see the quality, read the manifesto, and know what to do in under two minutes.

## **Phase 2 — Collect the evidence (weeks 1–3)**

**Goal:** turn spectators into participants.

* Build the smallest complete Archive of No flow.  
* Seed 25–40 varied entries from the founders and trusted early contributors.  
* Implement moderation, redaction, takedown, permanent URLs, and automated share cards.  
* Test the entire flow on a phone with a non-technical person.  
* Put **Submit your rejection** on every site and social profile.

**Exit condition:** a stranger can submit in a few minutes, moderators can publish safely, and the result is worth sharing.

## **Phase 3 — Manufacture inevitability (weeks 3–8)**

**Goal:** create a repeatable publishing rhythm instead of a one-day launch.

Use a small number of recurring formats:

* **Rejection of the Week** — one Archive story.  
* **Ministry Decree** — one bureaucratic proclamation.  
* **Pontifical Bulls of Rejection** — decrees, encyclicals, and infallible refusals from Pope Rejectus IV.  
* **Dispatch from the Founding Fathers** — comics, origin stories, or field reports.  
* **The Parade of Almost** — periodic themed open call.

Launch with the two finished campaign posters, not all material at once. Each post should drive to one Archive entry or the submit page.

**Exit condition:** eight weeks of material can be scheduled without inventing the project again every morning.

## **Phase 4 — Recruit foreign cells (months 2–4)**

**Goal:** prove it belongs to more than its founders.

* Invite illustrators, rejected writers, performers, designers, job seekers, and small art communities to contribute.  
* Publish the Italian **RIFIUTAZIONISMO** edition first; add other languages only with committed editors/moderators.  
* Release a downloadable propaganda pack so people can print or repost approved material.  
* Prepare a compact press kit and pitch the human phenomenon plus the visual work—not “two men made a funny website.”  
* Run a themed online exhibition or legal physical pop-up before attempting a large event.

**Exit condition:** genuine submissions from at least 10 countries and recurring contributors who are not personal friends.

## **Phase 5 — Occupy culture, then fund it (months 4–12)**

**Goal:** make the movement visible in the physical world and financially self-sustaining without ruining the joke.

* Publish a limited **Archive of No** zine or annual **Book of No**.  
* Sell numbered poster editions, Ministry certificates, stamps, badges, and a small number of excellent garments.  
* Use preorder or print-on-demand until demand is proven; boxes of unsold T-shirts are not revolutionary.  
* Stage **The Parade of Almost**, gallery installations, readings, or projections only with permission and a documented safety/legal plan.  
* Offer collaborations only when Rejectionism retains editorial control. Do not let a recruitment platform turn it into a “resilience campaign.”

**Exit condition:** the project pays its hosting/production costs, contributors are credited, and the archive keeps growing without constant founder intervention.

# **8\. The next ten moves—in order**

1. Record the final primary/secondary logo decision.  
2. Recover the important missing visuals listed above.  
3. Create the proper vector and export pack.  
4. Confirm the four domains, redirects, renewal dates, and social URLs.  
5. Finish and publish the one-page rejectionism.co.uk front door.  
6. Finalize Archive of No submission, moderation, redaction, and share-page rules.  
7. Seed the Archive with 25–40 strong entries.  
8. Publish the two launch posters and founder banner as a coordinated opening campaign.  
9. Begin the weekly three-format content rhythm: Archive story, Ministry decree, Church/Founder lore.  
10. Review actual submissions and sharing after four weeks before building shops, extra sites, apps, or elaborate features.

# **9\. What not to do yet**

* Do not create a standalone Church website.  
* Do not build mandatory accounts, social networking, comments, likes, follower systems, or gamification into the Archive MVP.  
* Do not produce more logo concepts until the current identity is cleaned and exported properly.  
* Do not open a merchandise warehouse before an audience asks to buy something.  
* Do not launch an empty archive.  
* Do not use five slogans in the same composition.  
* Do not publish personal data from real rejection letters.  
* Do not allow the Ministry and Church to visually swallow the parent movement.  
* Do not make Rejectionism inspirational. The refusal to become a TED Talk is part of the art.

# **10\. Scoreboard**

Vanity traffic is not world domination. Track actions that prove participation and transmission.

| Stage | Signal that matters |
| :---- | :---- |
| Foundation | All canonical assets named, classified, backed up, and production-ready |
| Public launch | Visitors reach manifesto/founders and click through to Archive submission |
| Archive | Submission completion rate, moderation turnaround, approved entries, and takedown/error rate |
| Distribution | Percentage of published entries shared; repeat visitors; newsletter/social return traffic |
| Community | Repeat contributors, countries represented, collaborator-led collections |
| Cultural reach | Press mentions, exhibition invitations, legitimate remixes, citations, and unsolicited fan material |
| Sustainability | Hosting/production costs covered without compromising editorial control |

## **First conquest milestone**

**100 approved rejection stories, from 10 countries, with at least 25 submitted by people unknown to the founders.**

That is the moment Rejectionism stops being a private joke with excellent art and becomes a real public movement.

# **12\. Maintenance ritual**

Update this HQ whenever:

* a domain is acquired, redirected, launched, or abandoned;  
* a visual becomes official, is superseded, or receives a new production export;  
* a canonical slogan, title, or character changes;  
* a roadmap phase is completed;  
* a new recurring campaign begins;  
* the Archive reaches a milestone.

Every update should change the date at the top. Old decisions remain visible as archived history; they do not disappear into another chat.
